summary: CosmoBlip is an interactive, browser-based astrophysical discovery platform developed for the NASA Space Apps Planet X and SPHEREx challenge. Designed to bridge the divide between professional hyperspectral survey pipelines and public scientific exploration, CosmoBlip transforms NASA’s 102-band near-infrared survey architecture into an intuitive visual cockpit accessible from any web browser—without requiring users to install specialized astronomical image viewers, write command-line scripts, or parse raw Flexible Image Transport System (FITS) data cubes.By uniting temporal animation (multi-epoch time-lapse playback, difference imaging, and proper-motion trails) with spectral decomposition (six detector-aligned infrared lenses, real-time 102-band spectral energy distribution plotting, and dynamic color–brightness cluster mapping), CosmoBlip empowers researchers, educators, students, and citizen scientists to detect hidden cosmic phenomena. Users can hunt for ultra-cold brown dwarfs, high-proper-motion nearby stars, pulsating variable giants, and potential distant outer Solar System bodies such as Planet X candidates—all through an approachable, guided interface backed by real astronomical coordinates and NASA/IPAC Infrared Science Archive (IRSA) protocols.
details:
Project Details (Copy-Paste Ready for NASA Space Apps Submission)

What It Does & How It Works

CosmoBlip (cosmoblip.earth) is a public, browser-based interactive discovery platform built for the Planet X and SPHEREx challenge. It transforms NASA’s 102-band near-infrared spectral survey data into an intuitive visual cockpit for both researchers and everyday citizen scientists—eliminating the need for command-line astrophysics software or specialized FITS viewers.

The platform is organized into four core interactive workspaces:

  1. 3D Space Tour & Cosmic Log: Users launch into an interactive WebGL 3D Solar System where they can orbit planets, zoom, quick-fly between celestial bodies, and explore an 18-card rotating SPHEREx Cosmic Log explaining infrared astronomy concepts.
    • Animate an 8-epoch time-lapse sky patch (640×640) to observe celestial motion and brightness changes chronologically.
    • Tune across SPHEREx’s 6 detector lenses (0.75 µm to 5.0 µm) and switch between specialized View Styles: Colour Mix (false-color thermal mapping from blue to red), Spot Change (difference imaging that subtracts stationary stars to isolate pulsing variables and moving objects), and Trails (connecting all 8 epochs into dotted proper-motion paths).
    • Click any source to inspect its 102-band Infrared Fingerprint (color-coded by detector lens with a live wavelength tracking marker) alongside a dynamic Colour & Brightness Map where stars, cold brown dwarfs, galaxies, and asteroids separate into distinct clusters in real time.
  2. Junior Space Explorer Manual & 1-Click Missions: An illustrated, zero-jargon field guide featuring four 1-click Space Missions that automatically configure the telescope’s target, lens, zoom, and view style to demonstrate real astrophysical phenomena (hunting a chilly brown dwarf, spotting a speeding star, catching a blinking giant star, or resolving a twin star system).
  3. Observer Field Notes & Bug Board: A collaborative sticky-note board where users filter discoveries, log unusual spectra or UI feedback, and attach instant snapshots of their current sky view.

Benefits & Intended Impact

  • Democratizing Hyperspectral Space Data: SPHEREx collects spectral data across more than 450 million galaxies and 100 million Milky Way stars, but raw 102-channel FITS cubes are invisible to the human eye and intimidating to non-specialists. CosmoBlip makes multi-epoch infrared exploration accessible in a single click.
  • Accelerating Citizen-Science Discovery: By combining time-lapse motion tracking (Trails and Spot Change) with spectral cluster isolation, CosmoBlip empowers students, educators, and amateur astronomers to help flag fast-moving nearby objects, ultra-cold brown dwarfs, variable stars, and potential distant Planet X candidates.
  • Classroom & STEM Engagement: The 3D Solar System tour and 1-click guided missions turn abstract concepts—like infrared wavelengths, molecular absorption, and proper motion—into hands-on visual experiments.

Tools, Coding Languages, Hardware & Software Used

  • Frontend & Visualization: JavaScript / TypeScript, HTML5 Canvas (custom 640×640 multi-epoch image compositor, 640×400 102-band spectral plotter, and 600×380 Colour-Magnitude scatter engine), WebGL / Three.js (interactive 3D Solar System environment), and CSS3.
  • Backend & Astronomical Data Processing: Python, FastAPI, Astropy (World Coordinate System alignment, FITS metadata handling, and continuum subtraction), and NumPy.
  • NASA Data & APIs: NASA/IPAC Infrared Science Archive (IRSA) Simple Image Access (SIA) and catalog protocols, SPHEREx 102-band wavelength specifications ($0.75\text{–}5.0\text{ }\mu\text{m}$), and JPL/Caltech mission documentation.
  • Deployment & Collaboration: Cloud web hosting (cosmoblip.earth), Git/GitHub version control, and standard laptops/browsers for testing across desktop and mobile viewports.

Creativity & Key Factors Considered by Our Team

  • Bridging Time and Chemistry in One Interface: Traditional sky viewers display static broadband images, while spectroscopic tools display complex 1D graphs. CosmoBlip creatively unites 8-epoch temporal animation with 6-lens infrared filtering so users literally watch hot stars fade away at $5\text{ }\mu\text{m}$ while hidden cold worlds pop into view.
  • Eliminating Cognitive Overload: Rather than overwhelming users with 102 separate wavelength sliders, we grouped SPHEREx’s 102 channels into its 6 physical detector lenses for rapid visual filtering while preserving all 102 data points in the object’s spectral fingerprint chart.
  • Accessibility & Performance Trade-offs: Because streaming full-sky FITS cubes live in a browser requires heavy bandwidth, we designed a targeted spatial cutout architecture backed by pre-indexed benchmark targets for instant playback, paired with plain-language labels (Spot Change, Colour Mix, Trails) so first-time users can make real discoveries within seconds.
